findings.title: A PIP's request carries `${subject.permissions}` only when some condition of the tenant also reads subject.permissions; otherwise the placeholder is ABSENT and goes out as null

In a url the difference is a call or no call.

evidence.text: internal/regogen/local.go:79-80 computes the value only for a reference of the module: `case spectables.KindSubjPermissions: v = m.permissions(req)`; local.go:96-100 gives every other placeholder `Resolved{State: spectables.StateAbsent}`. pipPlaceholders (pipcall.go:147-159) puts `["subj","permissions"]` among the placeholders, and placeholderValue (pipcall.go:480-483) reads it from req.Values.

Probe (axis) at 1872c610 (Generate + SubjectOf + ResolveSubject + Project; MAPPING subject.permissions granting p1 to admin; token with role admin): condition `subject.g == 'x'` sends `{"requestAttributes": {"p": null}}`; `subject.g == 'x' OR subject.permissions CONTAINS 'zz'` sends `{"requestAttributes": {"p": ["p1"]}}`. Neither depends on the other conditions of the tenant.

findings.proposed_solution: Decide the value of a placeholder by its source where the request is built, not by whether a reference of the module filled req.Values: compute subject.permissions from the MAPPING tables for a placeholder too (the specification's reading), or give null to every placeholder of a MAPPING, GENERAL, or FILTERED source and name that reading among the knobs pipcall.go lists.
findings.retest: With a MAPPING subject.permissions that grants p1 and a GENERAL whose requestAttributes hold `{"p": "${subject.permissions}"}`, the request body is the same whether or not another condition of the tenant reads subject.permissions; the same holds for the placeholder inside a nested object and in the url's query (`?p=${subject.permissions}`), where both conditions either call the PIP or both fail it.

findings.title: check/filter substitutes the predicate of a simplified policy only until one policy allows every row, so the same simplified policies answer ALLOW in one order and DENY in the other when a later predicate has a placeholder no source renders
findings.problem: A placeholder the filter cannot render (an undeclared name, a GENERAL PIP whose call failed, `${subject.permissions}` without a MAPPING PIP, `${subject.permissionScope.x}` outside an iterate) denies the whole filter, but only when `substituter.term` runs: `simplified` returns ALLOW at the first policy that allows every row and skips `term` for a policy whose condition is false or unknown, and `policy` skips it for such a rule. The specification's agent profile builds the term of every matching policy, and of every rule whose target holds, before it reads the condition, and answers DENY in each case.

evidence.text: internal/regogen/filteralg.go:357-359: `if c.v == 1 {` / `return pair{a: allRows}, nil` — returns before the later policies of the operation reach `e.sub.term` at :350.

findings.title: check/filter calls the GENERAL PIPs of policies for every resource type and operation, so a filter of one type waits AUTHZ_PIP_TIMEOUT for a PIP that only another type's policy reads

findings.title: check/filter answers ALLOW for `subject denied 'OP' on resource` when OP's decision depends on a target over the resource, so it admits the rows check/resource denies
findings.problem: In check/filter a policy, set, or rule target that reads the resource leaves the decision for OP neither permit nor deny on the request, but `uncertain` ignores targets, so the leaf reads only the lower bound `_loP`. That bound is false, `subject denied` is true on every row, and an ALLOW rule over it admits every row, including those where OP is allowed and check/resource denies, with no failed source involved. ADR-0099 R1 forbids the filter to admit a row the check denies.

evidence.text: Ran the reproducer at 1872c610 (`go test ./internal/regogen -run <probe>`): `check/filter(read) = ALLOW; check/resource denies the rows with d = 'y'`.

A differential over generated trees (the metamorphic tree generator, predicates folded into conditions as ADR-0099 R1 states, every check/filter answer evaluated as RSQL on 24 rows of columns a, b, c, d) found this as the only shape where the filter admits a row that both the folded and the plain check/resource deny: 1 of 1500 trees with seed 7, shrunk to the two sets of the reproducer.

gen.go:839-843: `// a decision that reads no unknown value has hi equal to lo, so the leaf is two-valued and reads lo alone` / `hi, three := name+"_hiP", g.uncertain(g.decRoots[name])`. gen.go:886-890: `uncertain` looks only at rule conditions, iterate, and unknown nodes, and says `A three-valued target does not split the bounds, as an undefined target gives both bounds of the node's body with its permit taken away`; in check/filter a target over the resource is not undefined on a row where it holds.

A condition over the resource in the same place (`resource.d == 'y'` as the write rule's condition) gives DENY, which is sound: the leaf of leaf.go:153 is three-valued, so only targets are missed. The `subject allowed` leaf under a DENY rule gives DENY too (narrower, sound); only `subject denied` reads the missing upper bound as a permit that never happens.
Neighbor of round-1 F19 and F77 (fixed in a0487937), which covered a decision with a failed source; this one has no failed source.

findings.title: Whether a jsonPath that Jayway does not compile selects nothing or leaves the subset depends on the order of its steps: `.x[:][?(@.a.b == 1)]` selects nothing, `.x[?(@.a.b == 1)][:]` is refused
findings.problem: Jayway refuses the whole path in either order, so legacy reads the attribute as absent in both; the agent isolates the policy that holds the second form as unsupported. The same holds between the parts of a filter's `||` or `&&` (filter.go:79-89).

evidence.text: Probe test at 1872c610 (internal/jsonpath): Compile(".x[:][?(@.a.b == 1)]") compiles and selects missing; Compile(".x[?(@.a.b == 1)][:]") and Compile(".x[?(@.a.b == 1)][99999999999]") return `jsonpath: unsupported path: ...: filter "@.a.b == 1"`; Compile(".x[?(@.a.b == 1 || @.c == 1𝟏)]") is unsupported, Compile(".x[?(@.c == 1𝟏 || @.a.b == 1)]") compiles and selects missing.

internal/jsonpath/jsonpath.go:240-249 defers only an errGoRegex step (`if errors.Is(err, errGoRegex) { ... continue }`) and returns any other unsupported step at once (`return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %q: %w", ErrUnsupported, path, err)`), before a later step can report errJaywayRefuses; internal/jsonpath/filter.go:79-89 does the same between the parts of && and ||.

Jayway compiles a nested filter path such as `@.a.b == 1`, and refuses `[:]` and an index beyond the int range for the whole path (the specification's jp_empty_slice COMPILE_ERROR), so the order of the steps does not change what legacy does.

Verifier probe at 1872c610: Compile(".x[:][?(@.a.b == 1)]") returns nil error; Compile(".x[?(@.a.b == 1)][:]") returns `jsonpath: unsupported path: ".x[?(@.a.b == 1)][:]": filter "@.a.b == 1"`. At e2c7029e the compile loop had no refused path (no errJaywayRefuses), so the order dependence is new.

findings.proposed_solution: Decide "Jayway refuses this path" over the whole path: keep the first unsupported error of any kind, as the errGoRegex branch already does, return the refused path when any later step or filter part refuses, and return the unsupported error only where no step refuses.
findings.retest: Compile(".x[?(@.a.b == 1)][:]") and Compile(".x[?(@.a.b == 1 || @.c == 1𝟏)]") return a path whose Select gives KindMissing, as their reordered forms do; so does CompileRootKey on the same paths.

findings.title: A PERMIT_OVERRIDES node whose denied rows are unknown passes them up whole, so an ancestor under PERMIT_UNLESS_DENY or DENY_OVERRIDES drops the rows its own ALLOW rule keeps, and check/filter answers DENY where check/resource allows
findings.problem: Under PERMIT_OVERRIDES the denied rows are ∪D ∖ ∪A (ADR-0099 R2), so where a child's denial is unknown (a DENY rule under a target over a failed PIP) the rows a sibling ALLOW rule allows are still not denied. `denied` returns the unknown d whole, and `subtract` in a PERMIT_UNLESS_DENY or DENY_OVERRIDES ancestor turns it into no rows, so the filter admits nothing where check/resource allows the sibling's predicate rows. This is neither pending owner case: no condition reads the failed PIP and no predicate substitutes it, and the same policy under a DENY_UNLESS_PERMIT set keeps `b!="y"`; ADR-0099 asks the filter not to narrow where the dialect can write the rows.

evidence.text: Ran the reproducer at 1872c610: `check/filter(read) = DENY`. Control, the same policy under a DENY_UNLESS_PERMIT set: `{Result:USE_FILTER_CONDITION Text:map[rsql:b!="y"]}`, so the rows are lost only at the ancestor's subtraction.

The differential over generated trees without resource atoms (seed 23, 500 trees) found this shape twice: s1809 (PERMIT_UNLESS_DENY over a PERMIT_OVERRIDES policy) and s607 (DENY_OVERRIDES set over a nested PERMIT_OVERRIDES set whose policy target is `subject.g == 'x'`), both with subject.g failed, check true on the rows of the ALLOW predicate, filter DENY.

filteralg.go:568-569: `case a.kind == rowsUnknown || d.kind == rowsUnknown || d.kind == rowsNot || e.approx:` / `return d`; filteralg.go subtract: `case d.kind == rowsAll || d.kind == rowsUnknown || e.approx:` / `return none`.
Commit d297314a ("deny under PERMIT_OVERRIDES only the rows not allowed") made this subtraction for a known d; an unknown d is the same input class one step further.

findings.title: Does legacy print a list or an object nested inside a structure as Jackson's JsonNode.toString does? evidence.text: encode.go:104-107 writes U+2028 and U+2029 as `\u2028` and `\u2029`; encode.go:92-95 writes other control characters as `\u00` plus lower-case hex; `Number` is written as the document wrote it (encode.go:54-55).
